Does it work for ipad? Any games you would recommend?

Not sure if it works for iPad or not, but some game recommendations:

  • Final Fantasy Advance series: FF IV-VI remade with new translations, content, and bug fixes, but worse music and washed out graphics.
  • Final Fantasy Tactics Advance: Not as good as the original FF:Tactics, but still a great game
  • Advance Wars: Excellent turn based strategy games.
  • Fire Emblem: Tactical Strategy RPGs. Two were released in America (titled Fire Emblem and FE: Sacred Stones) and a Japan-only sequel for the one titled Fire Emblem in the US. The last one has a translation patch out there though.
  • Mother 3: Haven't played this one personally, but its considered one of the greatest RPGs of all time. It was Japan-only, but there is a translation patch readily available.
  • Golden Sun: A lesser known RPG series, but well worth playing for its unique class system and good story. The story spans two games and are connected via a password system (or linking if you have another iOS device available).
  • The Sims series: Even if you don't like the main series games, the GBA games might be worth checking out. They're RPG/Adventure games with charming characters and stories. The GBA ones are Bustin' Out, the Urbz, and Sims 2.

I tried to stick to games that work well with touchscreen controls, hence all the RPGs. Some that wouldn't work as well are the Donkey Kong Country series, The Super Mario Advanced series, Banjo-Kazooie: Grunty's Revenge (the last proper Banjo game), and the Megaman Zero series.

EDIT: Added the SIms, and Bolded titles for readbility.
I have has trouble with some of the games I have downloaded not opening. Do you have any advice?

What is their format? If it's zip or .7z, you might need to extract them; I'm not sure if GBA4iOS can read .7z files and may have trouble with certain .zips. Try this:

  1. Download the ROM on your computer
  2. Extract it until you get a .GBA or .GBC file. If it's a zip file Windows can handle it, but if it's a .7z file you'll need a special program.
  3. Load the GBA/C file into Dropbox or any other cloud file service that you can access from Safari on your phone.
  4. Access the file you uploaded from Safari and chose to "Open in GBA4iOS". this should add the game to your menu and it should play fine.
